skill.name: azure-rbac
skill.description: Find the least-privileged Azure RBAC role for an identity. Generate Azure CLI and Bicep role assignments, including custom-role guidance when needed.
skill.summary: Select and assign least-privileged Azure RBAC roles.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: Both static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline-code delimiters around an Azure permission name. The skill contains no executable shell or Ruby command at those locations.

static_findings.snippet: To assign RBAC roles to identities, you need a role that includes the `Microsoft.Authorization/roleA

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks delimit an Azure permission name in Markdown prose; no shell, Ruby, interpolation, or execution mechanism exists.
The backticks format the same Azure permission inside a Markdown list item; the line contains no executable command or dynamic input.

content.value_statement: Selecting an Azure role with excessive permissions increases security risk. This skill recommends minimal roles and prepares Azure CLI and Bicep assignments.
actual_capabilities: Finds a minimal built-in Azure role for requested permissions.
Recommends a custom role when no built-in role matches.
Generates Azure CLI commands for role assignments.
Produces Bicep guidance for role assignment resources.
Explains which roles can grant Azure RBAC access.
limitations: Requires access to the referenced Azure documentation and generation tools.
Does not verify the current Azure tenant, identity, scope, or assignments.
Generated commands and Bicep require review before deployment.
Does not execute role assignments or confirm deployment results.

use_cases.title: Grant Storage Read Access
use_cases.description: Identify the minimal role for an application that only reads blobs at a defined scope.

use_cases.title: Automate Role Assignments
use_cases.description: Prepare Azure CLI and Bicep assignments for managed identities in repeatable infrastructure deployments.

use_cases.title: Design a Custom Role
use_cases.description: Define limited permissions when available built-in roles grant more access than required.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Built-In Role
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the least-privileged Azure role that lets [identity] perform [actions] on [resource scope]. Explain why it fits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with a clear identity, action, and scope.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Azure CLI Assignment
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend the minimal role for [identity] at [scope], then prepare the Azure CLI assignment command.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a command after selecting a suitable role.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Bicep Assignment
prompt_templates.prompt: Create Bicep guidance assigning the least-privileged role to [principal] at [scope]. Include required identifiers and dependencies.
prompt_templates.scenario: Add an RBAC assignment to infrastructure code.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Custom Role Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare built-in roles for [required actions]. If none fit, define a minimal custom role and provide CLI and Bicep assignment guidance.
prompt_templates.scenario: Evaluate permissions before creating a custom role.

output_examples.input: A managed identity must read blobs from one storage account.
output: Recommended role: Storage Blob Data Reader.
Scope: the specific storage account or narrower container scope.
Next step: review generated Azure CLI and Bicep assignments.

output_examples.input: Which role lets an operator create role assignments without full resource control?
output_examples.output: Use User Access Administrator when role assignment is the only required administrative capability. Owner grants broader resource control.

output_examples.input: No built-in role matches a limited set of resource actions.
output: Compare requested actions against current built-in roles.
Define a custom role containing only required actions.
Review assignable scopes before generating deployment guidance.

best_practices: Use the narrowest practical assignment scope.
Confirm required actions before selecting a role.
Review generated commands and Bicep through normal change controls.
anti_patterns: Do not assign Owner when a narrower role meets the requirement.
Do not create a custom role before checking built-in roles.
Do not deploy generated assignments without validating identity and scope identifiers.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy Azure role assignments?
faq.answer: No. It provides recommendations and generated guidance for review and deployment.

faq.question: Can it recommend built-in Azure roles?
faq.answer: Yes. It searches Azure documentation for a minimal role matching the requested permissions.

faq.question: When does it suggest a custom role?
faq.answer: It suggests a custom role when no built-in role matches the required permissions closely enough.

faq.question: Does it generate Azure CLI commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It can generate role assignment commands after identifying the role, identity, and scope.

faq.question: Does it support Bicep?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides Bicep guidance for adding role assignments to infrastructure deployments.

faq.question: Which permission is required to assign roles?
faq.answer: The granting identity needs Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write, usually through User Access Administrator, Owner, or a suitable custom role.
